foreign_boundary: Pinned external SQLite C plus mechanical libc filesystem, allocation and pthread synchronization; no business policy
entry: uint64_t trnm_task_provider(void *opaque, uint64_t op, const unsigned char *request, uint64_t size, unsigned char *output, uint64_t capacity)

lifetime.new: void *trnm_task_provider_new(void); null on real allocation or mutex construction failure
lifetime.reset: uint64_t trnm_task_provider_reset(void *opaque); finalize every retained statement, then close_v2 each retained database and close each retained descriptor; returns actual resource count
lifetime.free: void trnm_task_provider_free(void *opaque); accepts null, resets resources and destroys mutex
assumptions: Opaque capability was returned by new and is still live.
Callers serialize use by enter/leave or equivalent exclusive typed ownership.
Input/output point to distinct live correctly sized buffers; output does not alias retained SQLite data.
HIA alone decides SQL, transaction order, error mapping, connection flags and resource lifetime; no validation booleans are consumed.
File descriptors returned by op17 belong to this exact live context; op18, op19 and op29 reject unretained, cross-context, and already-closed descriptors.
Production owners in one process must share one exact SQLite provider image; independently linked qualification executables/libraries run in separate processes.

wire.scalar_response: 24 bytes: u64 code; u64 first; u64 second
wire.value_response: 24-byte header: u64 zero; u64 SQLite type; u64 byte length; followed by raw bytes

types.1: INTEGER, signed i64 bits in eight bytes
types.3: TEXT, exact raw SQLite text bytes

wire.function_return: Required output byte length; UINT64_MAX rejects invalid framing/capability; UINT64_MAX-1 reports private bridge allocation failure. Neither sentinel is any original SQLite, OS, or business error.
wire.insufficient_capacity: Mutating calls check capacity>=24 before effects; variable results only inspect retained objects and may be retried after growth.
wire.limits: Only actual SQLite/int ABI widths and allocation/OS bounds. No task count, path byte count, record count or database capacity is invented.

operations.request: u64 descriptor; u64 requested byte count
operations.response: errno; actual byte count; zero; followed by exactly that many bytes. Only this context's retained descriptor. With header capacity present, capacity<24+requested returns 24+requested before calling read. Short reads, EOF zero and EINTR are returned unchanged; HIA owns retry/read_exact policy. No pread substitution, implicit seek, or extra request-size cap.
